summary.title: Financial Planning & Analysis
summary.one_liner: GitLab's public FP&A handbook explains how the company runs its annual operating plan, long-range outlook, business planning, monthly close and variance analysis, quarterly forecasts and guidance, and headcount forecasting.
takeaways: The AOP is a three-statement, non-GAAP bottoms-up annual plan approved by the board, with revenue forecast from the bookings plan and expenses planned by headcount and vendor.
The Long Range Outlook is a top-down three-to-five year strategic and financial plan refreshed annually and updated quarterly.
Monthly close runs on an 8-day accounting close with variance and flux analysis, targeting revenue and EBIT variance within +/-2% quarterly.
Headcount Forecast lives in Workday Adaptive, and the Hiring Plan is the subset of planned and backfill positions maintained by Finance Business Partners.
summary.summary: This GitLab handbook page describes the mission, objectives, and processes of the company's FP&A team. It covers the Annual Operating Plan and its planning steps, the Long Range Outlook, business plan requirements, and the monthly and quarterly close, forecast, and variance review cycle. It also covers quarterly guidance and the headcount forecast and hiring plan. The page is an internal process reference with specific milestones, deadlines, and materiality targets rather than a tutorial.
